mechanism_narrative: The current federal funds rate of 2.4% is historically associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. This low rate environment compresses discount rates and supports equity valuations, leading to positive forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS is at or below 2.4% over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS is above 4.5% over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is rising (FEDFUNDS increase > 0.2% in 3 months) and CPIAUCSL is rising (CPIAUCSL increase > 0.3% in 3 months), the combined signal indicates an overheating economy and imminent rate hikes, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rise > 0.2% and CPIAUCSL rise > 0.3% in 3 months
failure_condition: The interaction signal (FEDFUNDS rise > 0.2% and CPIAUCSL rise > 0.3% in 3 months) fails to predict negative returns in more than 50% of instances over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: In high unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 5%), the Federal Reserve is likely to implement monetary easing, which supports equity valuations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE is above 5% over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts below 1200 thousand units signal weak demand and potential economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when HOUST is below 1200 over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production below 105 (2017=100) indicates a contraction in manufacturing output, signaling economic weakness and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO is below 105 over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in residential fixed investment (RSAFS) and industrial production (INDPRO) signals a broad-based economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decline > 0.5% and INDPRO decline > 0.3% in 3 months
failure_condition: The interaction signal (RSAFS decline > 0.5% and INDPRO decline > 0.3% in 3 months) fails to predict negative returns in more than 50% of instances over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: CPIAUCSL above 260 (index value) indicates high inflation, which triggers monetary tightening and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL is above 260 over the last 5 years.
